suggestions.quote: By the time he left school, he'd used up 93% of his in-person time with his parents (c01).
suggestions.fix: Too long for one breath (17 words, about 8 s at 1.1x). Split it into takes: "By the time he left school? Ninety-three per cent. Of his time with his parents, in person. Used up." Put 'ninety-three per cent' in say.yaml. The last fragment is a complete thought, so the line still lands.

Alone it has no antecedent: the planted "She always is" was five minutes earlier. Restore the packaging version: "She's still at the door. Of course she is." It stays one real line inside the last image and pays off line 39. Keep the hushed, warm direction.

suggestions.quote: Next morning. A new city. Counters everywhere.
suggestions.fix: The held shot already shows counters bobbing over the heads, so "Counters everywhere" narrates the picture. Cut it: "Next morning. A new city." and let the amused beat fall on the picture.

suggestions.quote: Everyone you know has one. The times you'll meet in person again, if your plans stay as they are.
suggestions.fix: Reads like an essay (19 words, one clause chain). Spoken form: "Everyone you know has one. The times you'll meet again. In person. If your plans stay as they are."
Add to say.yaml: "Diwali" → "di-WAH-lee". Do the same for "dal" in line 162 ("More dal.") → "dahl", so the one-word take doesn't misfire.

suggestions.quote: 64% picked it as their favourite. Whatever the flavour (c02).
suggestions.fix: The spoken form is in say.yaml ("sixty-four per cent"). Make the take quick and light, as an aside. "Whatever the flavour" can start with a lifted, amused "Any flavour." so the two fact lines don't read as a lecture.

Counter values are read aloud while the TAG and the counter show them (lines 22, 77, 89, 158). It works as a device, but give each its own take with a distinct reading: "Nine." cold and quiet, "Forty-two." a beat before, so they don't pile up as flat repeats.

keep.quote: You thought it would drop when you left. It drops when you walk in.
"Let's see" was a plan. And it did the maths.
It wasn't her clock. It was your timetable.
